reviews.text: Thank you very much for everything.

I underwent surgery for a Grade 3 hernia.

It was a rare type of hernia and required a technically demanding surgery, but I was able to walk normally immediately after the operation. I was completely unable to walk before, so I'm incredibly relieved.

The doctor and nurses were very kind, and their explanations were easy to understand. They also maintain close communication with my primary care physician, which is very reassuring.

I feel lucky to have found such a wonderful hospital.

I requested an MRI and CT scan for diagnosis and surgery. Considering my dog's condition, they suggested surgery the next day, and the post-operative explanation was thorough, including a video of the surgery (they asked beforehand if I wanted to watch it, as it might be something people would want to look away from). My dog, who was crying loudly, lying down, and trembling in pain, became so energetic after the surgery that he was jumping around happily, and now, two years later, he seems to have no pain at all. Although it always seems to be busy, there are multiple doctors, nurses, and receptionists working together, and I remember being seen on time if I had an appointment. It's a hospital where the reason for the busyness is understandable.

My six-month-old Toy Poodle started limping with her left front leg raised after playing at the dog park. I took her to our regular vet for an examination and X-ray. The vet suspected a problem with her joint and referred us for further testing, which led to our visit here.

Before coming here, we had stopped giving her pain medication and were observing her condition. She didn't seem to be in pain and was otherwise healthy, so our vet had mentioned the possibility of a CT scan or even arthroscopic surgery. I was incredibly anxious and worried, wondering if such major tests were really necessary when she seemed so healthy, and what the outcome would be.

We arrived at the clinic and Dr. Kikuchi examined her.

Dr. Kikuchi listened carefully to my concerns, performed a physical examination, and took six X-rays.

He was a very kind doctor, explaining everything thoroughly, which made me feel completely at ease.

After detailed X-rays and a physical examination, it was determined that there were no abnormalities in the bones or joints, and that she might have simply strained a muscle. She was allowed back to go for walks.

Dr. Kikuchi's explanation was very clear and easy to understand, and I left feeling relieved. It was a bit of a long journey, but I'm so glad we came to the clinic and had our dog thoroughly examined.
Our whole family has been talking about how we'd like to have Dr. Kikuchi examine our dog if anything happens.
Our puppy is only six months old, so we don't know what might happen in the future, but this is definitely a hospital we'd like to rely on.
Thank you so much, Dr. Kikuchi.

I took my Papillon dog to this hospital for patellar luxation.

It's a popular hospital, so there's a bit of a wait, but they gave a very thorough and attentive examination, and suggested options that would minimize stress on my dog.

Thanks to their appropriate advice, the patellar luxation symptoms have subsided without surgery.

It's a bit of a distance from my home, but I trust the doctor, so I always take my dog ​​here for any joint problems.

Dear Mr./Ms. Takamasa Ito, This is YPC Tokyo Animal Orthopedic Hospital.

Thank you very much for your kind review.

It is a great encouragement to all of our staff.

We will continue to provide you with our best support, so please feel free to contact us anytime.

Last fall, I went to get an X-ray to check the condition of my dog's patella.
I was referred by my family doctor, and I mentioned at the appointment and during the examination that my dog ​​is very fearful.
He had an X-ray because his left knee was bad, but they took X-rays of both legs, and as a result, his right leg hurt when he got home.
I went back to the examination the next day and was prescribed pain medication.
More than two months have passed, and he still sometimes lifts his right leg, so I'm seeing a different orthopedic surgeon.
I believe it was an accident caused by my fearful dog putting too much strain on me or resisting, but I never thought he would hurt himself just by being restrained.
Why did it get worse when we went for an examination?
His fearfulness got even worse, and he could barely go outside. Over the past few days, he's finally been able to go for walks, despite still trembling.
I feel so sorry for my dog ​​and am truly disappointed. I will never go there again.

Thank you so much for your excellent care during my dog's patellar luxation surgery (left knee, grade 4) and hospitalization.

The thorough explanations before and after the surgery, the detailed explanation and report of the surgical procedure with images during the operation, and the meticulous care until discharge—everything conveyed the doctor's thoughtfulness and sincerity, and I am filled with gratitude.

The staff were also always kind and reassuring, which eased my anxieties many times.

Thanks to you, my dog ​​was able to receive treatment with peace of mind, and I truly feel that this is a trustworthy hospital.

I am so glad I chose this hospital.

Thank you from the bottom of my heart.

I wanted to post a review sooner, but I wanted to wait until after my dog's 3-month checkup was successfully completed, so I'm writing this now.

My Toy Poodle is only 3 years old, but after nearly a month of observation at our regular vet with no improvement, they suspected a herniated disc and referred us to this hospital.

When I contacted them, I was able to get an MRI appointment for the very next day, so I went there first thing in the morning. As expected, the diagnosis was a herniated disc. Fortunately, my dog ​​could walk on his own and it was grade 1. Dr. Takahashi, the associate director, spent over an hour explaining everything to us, even though we're not experts, until we fully understood. He explained the advantages and disadvantages of both drug therapy and surgery, giving us, as pet owners, a choice. Ultimately, we chose surgery, and I still believe it was the right decision.

The costs were clear, and including the MRI, it came to just under 800,000 yen, but the result was very satisfying.

It's certainly not cheap.

However, the doctor himself contacted us after the surgery, explaining the details of the procedure and my dog's condition. I was very worried, but I was able to leave my dog ​​in their care with peace of mind.

I can't imagine what would have happened to my dog ​​if Dr. Takahashi hadn't examined him.

He's truly a top-notch orthopedic surgeon for dogs.

Now, four months after the surgery, seeing him running around so energetically, I'm truly grateful that we were able to have him treated at this hospital.

Dr. Takahashi, the veterinarians, nurses, and reception staff are all so kind whenever we visit. The short waiting time, even when it's busy, was also a big plus. Thank you very much.

A wonderful hospital. Wonderful staff.

This time, I was referred to this hospital by my family veterinarian for an MRI scan of my beloved cat. Dr. Takahashi was in charge.

Not only did the scan help identify the correct hospital, but we also received detailed advice on subsequent care. My cat and I are both very grateful.

I've always taken my previous dog and my current dog to Yamaguchi Pet Clinic for treatment.

However, recently they seem to want to switch to orthopedic care. They've stopped giving vaccinations, and when I inquired about health checkups or wanted my dog ​​examined because he wasn't feeling well,
they told me to ask my regular vet.

I've always considered Yamaguchi Pet Clinic my regular vet, and they should have records of it in their medical charts, but I felt like they were pushing me away, so I reluctantly went to find another vet.

I'm disappointed because I relied on them for so long.

I'm also really sorry that the person who recommended this clinic now has to find another one.

I'm angry at the reception staff's attitude, who have no understanding of the owner's suffering.

My dog ​​also had a herniated disc, and we were referred to this clinic for surgery. At first, they said it would cost less than 500,000 yen, but when we were discharged, the bill was over 600,000 yen. We were shocked when they told us so suddenly.

I was able to get an appointment on short notice, and I went to see the doctor.
The doctor explained everything carefully.
However, my blood test results were abnormal, so surgery wasn't possible.
The receptionist was extremely unpleasant!

Dear parkwing0905, This is YPC Tokyo Animal Orthopedic Hospital.
Thank you for your high rating.

I previously had surgery performed on my miniature dachshund for a herniated disc. The night before the surgery, he suddenly became unable to stand, so I took him to an emergency hospital where he was diagnosed with a grade 5 disc and told to come back the next day. They smoothly performed an MRI and, due to his condition, recommended surgery that day, which we had performed.

The veterinarians who treated him were very kind and explained everything clearly.

I appreciated that they clearly explained the risks involved, emphasizing the time-sensitive nature of the situation.

They also helped me consider post-operative care, and I am extremely grateful to the hospital staff. Thank you very much.

Dr. Kikuchi treated my dog ​​for a fractured elbow.

My regular hospital couldn't perform fracture surgery, so I was referred to a nearby orthopedic hospital that specializes in fractures. However, they said the fracture was quite difficult and would definitely leave permanent damage. Because the fracture was complex within the joint, they said it would be a blessing if my dog ​​could return to being able to put some weight on the leg, but they said that it was a level of treatment that would require treatment at a university hospital. I was a little hesitant to go to a university hospital, so I did some research and visited this hospital in Tokyo that specializes in orthopedics.

I called and they admitted my dog ​​the same day. Dr. Kikuchi examined him, and it was clear that the surgery would be quite difficult. His explanation of the possible complications was just as scary as at the previous hospital, but Dr. Kikuchi's explanations and approach to the surgery were very positive, and I felt I could trust him with the surgery.

In the end, the surgery was a great success, and my dog ​​is back to running around happily with no permanent damage. I'm so grateful to have found Dr. Kikuchi. Thank you so much.

My beloved cat was in an accident and suffered a serious back injury, which left him unable to walk. He was taken to the hospital and underwent surgery, but now he is able to go up and down the stairs. If I had not received care at this hospital, his prognosis might have been poorer and he might not have survived. I cannot thank you enough. Thank you so much!!!

The staff are very considerate to owners and provide kind, thorough explanations, which gives me great peace of mind.
I feel at ease knowing my dog ​​will be examined there.

Dear Serena, This is YPC Tokyo Animal Orthopedic Hospital.

Thank you for your feedback.

This time, we received treatment here through a referral from our regular veterinarian. Our dog underwent surgery using the TPLO method for a torn anterior cruciate ligament, and also had surgery for a patellar luxation that resulted from the procedure. The surgery was postponed once due to our dog's health, which worried us greatly, but thanks to the smooth communication with our regular veterinarian and the subsequent treatment, the surgery was successfully performed two weeks later. Both before and after the surgery, the explanations were concise and thorough, and although we were worried about general anesthesia for our elderly dog, the head veterinarian allowed us to entrust him to their care with peace of mind. The post-operative recovery went smoothly, including the removal of the stitches, and today, at the one-month check-up, everything was fine. The doctor said our dog is recovering well, and that his leg will get better and his muscles will develop from here on out, which was a great relief. Thank you so much. The advanced medical care, the skills, the head veterinarian, and all the staff were all excellent. We will be back for the three-month check-up. Thank you in advance.

My dog ​​wasn't feeling well, so I took him to this hospital on a referral. The associate director examined him.

The service was 100 points. I'm not really in a position to rate dogs, but...

He spoke to me sincerely and empathetically about my dog, treating him like family, which put me at ease.

I hope we never have to go to the hospital again, but if something happens, I would definitely rely on this doctor again.

The MRI was expensive, but the thorough examination I received more than made up for it.

Last year, my family's dog underwent surgery for a lumbar disc herniation, and we received a referral from our regular veterinarian. The clinic maintained excellent communication from pre-operative to post-operative stages, and we were able to communicate smoothly with our regular veterinarian after the surgery.

Surgery on a dog is a big deal, as the dog can't express its feelings, and the cost is significant, so we were very anxious. However, the surgeon who performed the operation gave concise and easy-to-understand explanations and answered our questions accurately. Some might perceive this conciseness and accuracy as cold or unkind, but it gave us the impression of a calm and composed medical professional (though not human), and we felt we could trust them to handle our beloved family member.

The wound was sutured very neatly, and now the surgical scar is almost invisible.

Now, our dog is completely recovered, running around and enjoying its favorite walks, so we are truly grateful.

Thank you very much.

I received excellent care when my dog ​​fractured its right front leg.

Their response was incredibly prompt and accurate, which was a huge help. …

Five years ago, my toy poodle underwent surgery for a herniated disc. Thanks to you, he is walking healthily with no major after-effects. I am extremely grateful for the miraculous treatment I received at the time.
